title: Galileo discovers the moons of Jupiter
summary: Looking through his improved telescope in Padua, Galileo Galilei saw small points of light beside Jupiter, which over the following nights he identified as moons orbiting it.
reason: Galileo had built telescopes far stronger than the first Dutch models and turned them systematically to the sky.
significance: Bodies orbiting another planet undermined the Earth-centered model and supported Copernicus.
